variant_answers.text: A description of the characters that matter: other characters may occur and are ignored, so the result depends only on the "(" and ")" characters, in order.
A non-empty string; the result for the empty string is unconstrained.

Order-insensitive matching: each "(" is paired one-to-one with some ")" anywhere in the string, so only the counts matter. CONTRADICTION with R-EX-4: under this reading ")(()" (two "(", two ")") would return True, but the example says False.

Full balance: the condition also requires that no ")" is left without a matching earlier "(" (a running count of "(" minus ")" never goes negative and ends at 0), so "())" and ")(" are not correctly bracketed.
The function returns any truthy value.
One direction only: the sentence constrains only the case where the condition holds; for other strings the result is not specified by this sentence (only the examples pin some of them to False).
